card.name: Kecak
card.tagline: Balinese 'monkey chant' Ramayana dance without instruments
card.profile: Kecak (also tari kecak) is a form of Balinese Hindu dance popularized in the 1930s, based on the Ramayana and performed primarily by men (Wikipedia). Also known as the Ramayana Monkey Chant, it is performed by a circle of as many as 150 performers wearing checked cloths who percussively chant 'cak' and move their arms, with no musical instruments. The performance depicts the battle in which the monkey-like Vanaras, led by Hanuman, help Prince Rama fight King Ravana. Kecak has roots in sanghyang, a trance-inducing exorcism ritual; in the 1930s German painter Walter Spies worked with dancer Wayan Limbak (and musician I Wayan Rindi) to develop it into a Ramayana spectacle.
card.insight: Scholar I Wayan Dibia argues the Balinese were already developing the cak chorus form before Spies arrived, with Limbak having incorporated baris movements into the leader's role in the 1920s (Wikipedia).
